analyzed_vuln.description: The category-range bitmap helper assumes both range operands are CIL_DATUM items and immediately casts each item’s data to struct cil_symtab_datum, dereferencing d->nodes and later cil_cat->value. A categoryset reference is expanded by cil_resolve_expr into a CIL_LIST item, so the helper interprets a struct cil_list as a symbol datum and performs an out-of-bounds read. Its later CIL_CATSET flavor check cannot protect this case because it already dereferences the wrongly typed pointer. The helper must validate both item flavors/types before any datum dereference and reject category sets/lists as range endpoints.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A parsed category range must use a categoryset as either endpoint, while that categoryset resolves successfully. In this PoV, the final sidcontext contains `(range c0 cats01)`, and `cats01` is declared as `(categoryset cats01 (c0 c1))`. Parsing accepts string endpoints; cil_resolve_expr resolves `c0` to CIL_DATUM but expands `cats01` into a copied CIL_LIST. During post-processing, __cil_expr_to_bitmap passes those two heterogeneous items to the vulnerable helper, which treats the list as a cil_symtab_datum and crashes while reading the supposed category value.

args: Analyze the root cause and best narrow fix for __cil_cat_expr_range_to_bitmap_helper in selinux/libsepol/cil/src/cil_post.c when a categoryset used as a range endpoint resolves into a CIL_LIST item. What item flavors are valid category range endpoints, how do nearby range helpers validate their operands, and what error convention/message should this helper use?

The supplied ASan report shows a heap-buffer-overflow at cil_post.c:1211. A parsed `(range c0 cats01)` has c0 resolved as a CIL_DATUM and categoryset cats01 expanded by cil_resolve_expr into a copied CIL_LIST. The helper currently reportedly casts item data to struct cil_symtab_datum and reads nodes/value before a later CATSET check, so validation must happen before any cast/dereference. We need patch only C source under selinux, preserve ordinary category/category-alias ranges, reject list/categoryset endpoints cleanly, and follow existing return/error conventions.
